prompt: Implement RefCheck.sameObject (are two references the exact same object, using ==) and RefCheck.sameContent (do they hold equal data, using a null-safe equals).
explanation: For reference types, == compares the references themselves -- it asks "are these the very same object?" -- while equals asks "do these objects hold the same data?". The tests build equal-but-distinct strings with new String(...) and StringBuilder precisely because string literals are interned and would share one object. The null-safe pattern (if a is null, the answer is whether b is also null; otherwise delegate to a.equals(b)) is exactly what java.util.Objects.equals does.
hints: sameObject is a single expression: a == b.
Calling a.equals(b) crashes when a is null -- handle the null case before delegating.
If a == null, return b == null; otherwise return a.equals(b). (java.util.Objects.equals does the same.)
